title: B$^3$-PWL: GPU-Batched Branch-and-Bound for Piecewise-Linear Optimization with SOS2 Constraints
claim: A CPU-managed search loop offloads whole batches of subproblems to a GPU solver pipeline, then uses the returned solutions to update the search.
layout: 2 large panels, left CPU to right GPU, numbered steps, dashed return arrows
description: The figure has two rounded panels side by side. The left blue panel, labeled CPU, shows the branch-and-bound loop. Step 1 is a search tree with explored, pruned and active nodes, where the N active leaves are selected. Step 2 packs LP1 to LPB into an orange batch box. Step 4 has three boxes: Prune (red), Update (green) and Branch (blue). The right green panel, labeled GPU, shows a batched cuPDLPx pipeline in three stages. Stage 1 is presolve and scaling, which turns a homogeneous batch into a heterogeneous one. Stage 2 is the batched PDHG iteration, where B²-SpMV blocks and projection operators update x and y in a loop. Stage 3 is postsolve and rescaling. Orange dashed arrows carry the batch to the GPU and the solutions back to the CPU, and a blue dashed arrow closes the outer loop. The eye starts at the CPU and GPU banners and the tree.
caption: Overall workflow for B3-PWL. Each round alternates between CPU-side B&B management and GPU-side batched LP solving. The CPU (left) selects N active subproblems from the search tree ( 1⃝), packs their LP relaxations into a batch ( 2⃝), and after the GPU returns solutions, verifies feasibility and updates the tree by pruning, updating the incumbent, or branching ( 4⃝). The GPU (right) executes a batched cuPDLPx pipeline ( 3⃝): per-task PSLP presolve and Ruiz scaling produce heterogeneous constraint matrices, batched PDHG iterations (built on our B2-SpMV kernel) run until convergence, and postsolve and rescaling yield primal-dual solutions for the entire batch. The outer loop continues until the active queue is empty or the global gap closes.
abstract: Piecewise-linear (PWL) optimization problems arise in many mixed-integer programming (MIP) optimization applications, including portfolio optimization, workforce scheduling, and resource allocation. But solving them to global optimality remains computationally expensive because branch-and-bound repeatedly solves LP relaxation subproblems. Existing solvers are largely CPU-centric, leaving the scalability of modern GPUs underutilized. Few prior GPU-accelerated branch-and-bound either targets neural network which is not suitable for general PWL optimization, or accelerates only auxiliary subroutines such as strong branching heuristics within CPU-centric MIP solvers. To bridge this gap, we propose B$^3$-PWL, a GPU-centric batched branch-and-bound framework for piecewise-linear optimization with Special Ordered Set of type 2 (SOS2) constraints. Our method solves batches of LP relaxation subproblems concurrently on the GPU using a first-order primal-dual solver, enabled by a specialized batched block-tiled sparse matrix kernel. To complement bound computation, we further introduce a unified feasibility search module that combines an SOS2 repair primal heuristic with a batched feasibility pump to rapidly obtain feasible incumbents and improve pruning efficiency. On a benchmark of 43 PWL-MIP instances, B$^3$-PWL achieves a 9.25x geometric-mean speedup over NVIDIA cuOpt while reaching high-quality feasible incumbents on every tested instance. On a public valve-point unit-commitment benchmark, it further outperforms NVIDIA cuOpt and the open-source CPU solvers SCIP and HiGHS, demonstrating the potential of first-order LP methods as the central engine of GPU-accelerated branch-and-bound.
